title: Move spoil piles back from a trench edge to the safe band
instruction: The spoil piles are too close to the trench. Move both of them to the far side of the trench, at least 0.6 m (6 cm in this 1:10 model) from its edge and wholly inside the red fence. Leave the near side clear for the workers.
context: OSHA requires excavated soil to be kept at least 2 ft (0.6 m) from a trench edge, since spoil near the edge can slide back in or collapse the wall onto workers. The pile has to go past an unmarked distance but stop short of the fence, so it can't simply be pushed as far as possible.
setup: A 1:10 scene on a wooden table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A trench, drawn as a dark band 30 mm wide with orange edge lines, runs side to side for 300 mm, its near edge 270 mm forward. A fixed red fence (8 x 300 x 25 mm) runs side to side 430 mm forward. Two brown spoil-pile blocks (40 x 40 x 30 mm, 60 g, foam) stand on the near side, 220 mm forward and 100 mm to each side, 30 mm from the trench edge.
scoring: Per pile: 0.5 if it stands upright on the table on the far side, its nearest point at least 60 mm beyond the trench's far edge, its farthest point short of the fence, and within the fence's 300 mm length; 0.15 if upright on the far side between the trench and the fence but inside the 60 mm setback; 0 otherwise (near side, in the trench, tipped, stacked or past the fence). Success once the score is 1.0 and both piles are still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Put both piles back on their start marks on the near side; the trench drawing and fence are fixed.
fidelity: A 1:10 model: the trench is painted on the table rather than dug, spoil piles are rigid blocks rather than loose soil, and the setback is checked from the pile's footprint. The fence is fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (step limit reached, no pile moved past the trench); demo: 1.0
